precepts.point: We were trodden down like the mire of the streets, and we are still being stomped on this very day.

precepts.text: The holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land. There's the precept for the mixing.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
To prove that Hosea's “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people” speaks of intermarriage, Ezra gives the precept: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.”

The holy seed is mixed: that is the word. Israel married the daughters of the strange people of the land, and the scripture calls it iniquity. There is the precept for the mixing.

So when Hosea says Ephraim is “a cake not turned,” it is describing what that mixing produced: part of Ephraim very light from mixing with Esau, and part very dark because they did not mix.

precepts.text: The holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.
precepts.point: The holy seed was mingled with the strange people of the land. Northern kingdom should learn its own history with the same zeal as the south's.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people”, sometimes willingly, sometimes not. You have knuckleheads who say that is only talking about their customs. It was biological and it was symbolic, dummy. The Bible defines the Bible, and Ezra shows what mixing means: “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles.”

We did not put away the strange people from the land. We sought after them, because of the ideology of whitening, of bettering the race. The pollutions of the Gentiles are their idolatry and their doctrines, and we became corrupt in our merchandise and commerce. All Israel had that propensity, but here the focus is the northern kingdom.

Read on: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.” When it says mixed himself among the people, it means the seed gets mixed. What is the seed? Sperm, semen. So when somebody comes to you with that BS, this is the scripture to put there: mixing means mixing.

It goes on: “and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.” All of us partook of that, and it is a sin to mix with the other nations. That is why Ephraim is a cake not turned: light on one side and dark on the other, all the different shades among the northern kingdom, and some of our own people with blonde hair and blue eyes whose father is Israel.

precepts.text: Even in the time of Ezra, Israel had not put away the strange people of the land, the Moabites among them; remember that it says the strange people of the land.
precepts.point: Were the sons of Israel supposed to take wives of the women of Moab while sojourning there? No; but remember what was just read at the end of Judges, that every man did that which was right in his own eyes. And this was not the first time Israel dealt with the women of Moab.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Israel kept dealing with the women of Moab long after this. Even in the time of Ezra: “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.”

The Moabites are named among the strange people of the land, and remember that it says the strange people of the land. Orpah and Ruth were of those strange people, and the sons of Israel took them to wife when the law said a Moabite should not enter into the congregation.

precepts.text: The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land; Ruth spoke of herself by that same word.
precepts.point: Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

precepts.why:
Ruth asked why Boaz took knowledge of her, “seeing I am a stranger”. She acknowledged what she was to Israel, and the scriptures use that same word of her people. “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.”

The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land. Ruth the Moabitess spoke of herself by that same word, a stranger, and knew her place before an Israelite.

precepts.text: For our sins and our fathers, we with our brethren and our kings and our priests were given up into the hands of the kings of the earth.
precepts.point: They take Manasseh among the thorns, bind him with chains, and carry him to Babylon. The kings of Israel that were once kings are brought down into captivity, exactly as the curses warned.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“And for our sins and our fathers’ we with our brethren and our kings and our priests were given up unto the kings of the earth, to the sword, and to captivity, and for a prey with shame, unto this day.”

The kings were not spared. Manasseh, king in Jerusalem, was taken “among the thorns”, bound “with fetters”, and carried “to Babylon”, because he and his people “would not hearken.” For their sins and their fathers’ sins, the kings of Israel were given up into the hands of the kings of the earth.

precepts.text: Ezra's great skill in the word came because he prayed and fasted to understand, and the Most High did great works through him.
precepts.point: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

precepts.why:
The fruit of Ezra's prepared heart is told in 1 Esdras: “Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.”

That great skill in the word came because he prayed and fasted to understand, and the Most High did great works through him. He came to Jerusalem “according to the good hand of his God upon him”, and having sought the law and done it, he taught all Israel, omitting nothing of the law and commandments.

precepts.text: Ezra blessed the Most High for putting it into the heart of the king, showing the good the heathen ruler does is the Lord moving him, not his own love for Israel.
precepts.point: The king grants him all this according to the good hand of his God upon him. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
Ezra saw the same thing in his day and knew where it came from: “Blessed be the only Lord God of my fathers, who hath put these things into the heart of the king, to glorify his house that is in Jerusalem”.

Ezra did not bless the king; he blessed the Most High for putting these things into the heart of the king. The good the heathen ruler does is the Lord moving him, not his own love for Israel. So when the king granted Nehemiah his letters and his timber, it was “according to the good hand of my God upon me”, the same hand that moved the king in Ezra's day.

precepts.text: The sons of Israel confess marrying strange wives of the nations, so the strange woman is a woman of the other nations.
precepts.point: The ways of a man are before the eyes of the Most High and He ponders all his goings. The wicked man's own iniquities take him and he is held with the cords of his sins, dying without instruction in the greatness of his folly.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
“And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?” The strange woman is a woman of another nation, and Israel confessed it as sin in the days of Esdras: “Then Jechonias the son of Jeelus, one of the sons of Israel, called out, and said, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord God, we have married strange women of the nations of the land, and now is all Israel aloft.”

The sons of Israel confess marrying strange wives of the nations of the land. Strange women are the women of the other nations, and marrying them was a sin against the Lord God.

That is the stranger whose bosom Solomon warns against. The strange woman carries a double meaning, a woman of another nation and a woman outside of your own wife, and here the first meaning is spelled out by Israel's own confession.

precepts.text: The gentiles are named as the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites, the same nations that did the stealing and hiding.
precepts.point: Now the stolen side: wicked nations robbed the heritage, hid the identity, and Edom exalted himself to claim it. That is why the ones calling themselves Jews today are called the synagogue of Satan, because they are not the people of the promise, they are the robbers who established the vision that they are Israel.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The gentiles are named: “the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.”

These are the nations that did the stealing and the hiding, the Edomites among them. To be part of the restitution you have to have lost something or had something stolen, and the scriptures show the opposite of these nations: they are the ones who robbed. So they are not gentiles being restored or grafted in; the restitution is for Israel.

precepts.text: The nations Israel was to destroy, Canaanites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites, are the Gentiles, proving Gentile can mean the scattered outcasts of Israel, not only the other nations.
precepts.point: People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.” The nations Israel was to destroy, the Canaanites, Moabites, Egyptians and Edomites, are here called the Gentiles.

That proves Gentile can mean the scattered outcasts of Israel, not only the other nations; the Gentiles who seek the ensign in Isaiah 11 are that remnant. So the man of Ethiopia is not proof that Philip went to the heathen. He was of the remnant of Israel in Kush.
